decision1.decision: Verified Player as Single Source of Truth
decision1.question: Why was Verified Player chosen as the single source?
decision1.evidence: Code structure shows VerifiedPlayerBuilder centralizing all player data
decision1.reasoning: Centralized canonical model aligns with FSRS v4 architecture principles
unknowns: No automated verification of single source enforcement
No metric registry to validate canonical constraints

decision2.question: Why is LLM layer the final layer?
alternativesConsidered: LLM earlier in pipeline for data enrichment
decision2.reasoning: Evidence-bound LLM requires verified data first, prevents LLM from generating facts
unknowns: No testing of LLM integration when implemented
Unknown if LLM will respect evidence boundaries

decision3.decision: Derived metrics not calculated in Presentation layer
decision3.question: Why are derived metrics calculated in Data Intelligence, not Presentation?
decision3.evidence: MetricExtractor calculates derived metrics, Presentation layer only consumes
decision3.reasoning: Maintains single source of truth, prevents calculation inconsistencies
unknowns: No performance testing of derived metric calculation at scale
Unknown if presentation layer needs on-demand calculations

weaknesses: No test coverage for architectural decisions
Production readiness not considered in current design
changesIfStartingOver: Add automated architectural validation from day one
Implement test-driven development for architectural decisions
Design for production readiness (observability, resilience) from start

Add metric registry to enforce single source of truth

chiefGuardianRecommendation.reasoning: Current architecture is sound but lacks automated validation and testing. This creates technical debt that will grow over time.

summary.architecturalConfidence: HIGH for Data Foundation, LOW for Football Intelligence, UNKNOWN for Decision/LLM
summary.overallAssessment: Architecture appears sound based on manual code review, but lacks automated validation and testing. This is acceptable for early development but must be addressed before scaling. The Chief Architecture Guardian recommends focusing on test coverage and automated architectural validation in the next sprint.
